title: Judgecraft from the margins: Decolonizing readings of Rwanda’s gacaca courts
abstract: This article develops the concept of gacaca judgecraft as a decolonial tool to critique the human rights discourse that was imposed on Rwanda’s gacaca courts. International human rights stakeholders have vehemently critiqued gacaca judges for lacking legal knowledge and impartiality. Adopting a decolonial lens, I critique this rights corpus using interviews with 80 Rwandan lay judges. I argue that community knowledge and emotions are essential elements of gacaca judgecraft. It is only by delinking from the rights paradigm that we can begin to see gacaca judges as producers of legal knowledge in their own right. I conclude that the concept of gacaca judgecraft can expand the possibilities for non-Western forms of (semi) legal reasoning.
